question.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)={x}_{1}(t)-2{x}_{2}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-{x}_{2}(t)+3,\end{aligned}\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform $L$ to both sides of each equation in our system, we get a system with variables ${X}_{1}(s)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}.$ In terms of the parameter $s,$ the solution of the new system is

${X}_{1}(s)=$ {{field-1}},$\,$
${X}_{2}(s)=\frac{3}{s(s+1)}.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we compute the Laplace transforms of both sides of each equation in our system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}L\{{x}_{1}^{′}(t)\}=L\{{x}_{1}(t)-2{x}_{2}(t)\} \\ L\{{x}_{2}^{′}(t)\}=L\{-{x}_{2}(t)+3\}\end{aligned}\,\,
$$

Using the derivative property of the Laplace transform, we obtain the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}sL\{{x}_{1}(t)\}-{x}_{1}(0)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}-2L\{{x}_{2}(t)\} \\ sL\{{x}_{2}(t)\}-{x}_{2}(0)=-L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}+3L\{1\}\end{aligned}
$$

which can be simplified to the following:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)+2={X}_{1}(s)-2{X}_{2}(s) \\ s{X}_{2}(s)-0=-{X}_{2}(s)+\frac{3}{s}\end{aligned}
$$

where ${X}_{1}(s)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L\{{x}_{2}(t)\},$ and we have used the fact that $L\{1\}=\frac{1}{s}.$

Now, solving the second equation for ${X}_{2}(s),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}s{X}_{2}(s) & =-{X}_{2}(s)+\frac{3}{s} \\ (s+1){X}_{2}(s) & =\frac{3}{s} \\ {X}_{2}(s) & =\frac{3}{s(s+1)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this in the first equation and solving for ${X}_{1}(s)$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)+2 & ={X}_{1}(s)-2{X}_{2}(s) \\ (s-1){X}_{1}(s) & =-2-2{X}_{2}(s) \\ (s-1){X}_{1}(s) & =-2-2(\frac{3}{s(s+1)}) \\ (s-1){X}_{1}(s) & =\frac{-2s(s+1)-6}{s(s+1)} \\ (s-1){X}_{1}(s) & =\frac{-2({s}^{2}+s)-6}{s(s+1)} \\ (s-1){X}_{1}(s) & =\frac{-2{s}^{2}-2s-6}{s(s+1)} \\ {X}_{1}(s) & =\frac{-2{s}^{2}-2s-6}{s(s+1)(s-1)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution of the new system in terms of parameter $s$ is 

$$
{X}_{1}(s)=\frac{-2{s}^{2}-2s-6}{s(s-1)(s+1)},\,{X}_{2}(s)=\frac{3}{s(s+1)}.
$$
